title: No structure sheet explicitly guarantees a one-entry maximum; S1 classifications are evidence-based
detail: All 37 official DSE IV structure sheets were read. None explicitly says 'one entry only' or promises a freezeout. The site nevertheless marks 53 event rows 'No second entry granted (S1 screen)' because each row's own sheet was read and no rule grants a second entry under the published S1 test; this is not a venue guarantee. The other 41 rows are classified as multi-entry under the same standard. Obtain a written event-specific cap from the tournament desk before treating any event as a guaranteed freezeout. Per-row evidence and the full standard are on the Verification page. Re-read 2026-11-19 (session 0a0d8e6b, data/0a0d8e6b/sheet_reread.json): the 22 structure sheets behind the 53 rows were read line by line. Their start times, buy-ins, guarantees, starting chips, late-registration closes, house fees and prize pools match the stored rows on 53 of 53 rows. None of the 22 sheets contains a written one-entry, maximum-entry, re-entry, rebuy or add-on sentence. The label therefore means 'no re-entry, rebuy or add-on wording found on the sheet', not 'written single-entry rule'. User decision: keep the label with this definition, or relabel these rows as 'no re-entry wording found'. The label was re-worded on 2026-11-19 ("No second entry granted (S1 screen)", PR #97) for exactly this reason: the pill states the result of the S1 screen, not a venue promise, and the old wording read as one. (session 6dba9b3c)

title: Whole-page hashing marked 48 of 96 official sources 'changed' on the first nightly run
detail: The monitor hashed every page as delivered. Casino pages carry per-request tokens and timestamps, so a 2-byte difference was recorded as a source change for half the ledger, and 'mark rows whose source changed' would have lit up rows whose values never moved. The monitor now compares extracted VALUES (scripts/monitor_b3be876c.py): the resort-fee sentence, the guarantee line, the registration-close line and the schedule row text. A row is marked only when one of those sentences changes; the raw page hash is kept as an informational column.

title: Wynn cancellation deadline: 72 hours was not reproducible; the live offer terms say 48 hours
detail: Several records (rate snapshots, Q14, F33) stated a Wynn cancellation deadline of '72 hours before arrival, per the Wynn terms page read 2026-11-17'. The Wynn terms page re-read on 2026-11-19 (offer DK26WLV2) says 'cancellations must be received at least 48 hours prior to arrival date or deposit will be forfeited', and its longer full-deposit and cancellation policy applies only to stays on 15-21 Nov, 29-31 Dec 2026 and 4-6 Jan 2027, not to 6-13 Dec. The 72-hour figure is therefore withdrawn and the record now carries 48 hours, labelled as the offer's terms. The standard (non-offer) rate policy was not read, so the planned rate's deadline is still unconfirmed. Re-read the booking-engine rate rules at quote time before any payment. Update 2026-11-19 (session f7676bd0): the 72-hour figure IS reproducible after all - from the Wynn booking engine's dated rate-details page for Dec 6-13, where the Flexible Getaway ($818 avg/night) and 'Your Fall to Have It All' ($688 avg/night) rate plans each print '72-Hour Cancellation (One Night's Room Rate and Tax Penalty Charged To Card)' and charge one night's room rate and tax at booking. So both figures exist, per rate plan: 72 hours on the two dated plans, 48 hours on offer DK26WLV2 and the Wynn Rewards Exclusive rate. Quote-time re-confirmation before payment still stands.
